content: It has happened dozens of times now that the attribution rubric required citing the roadmap and the documentation rubric rejecting references to the roadmap in the code. This should be clarified to avoid unnecessary back and forth. Filed here: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiReview/issues/130
Might be worth checking for other conflicts between rubrics more systematically.

I had Claude look into other common conflict and filed them as the following issues:

  • https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiReview/issues/132
  • https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiReview/issues/133

I've also seen this a lot in my own PRs.

Sometimes the goals of two review agents seem genuinely at odds (as in your example, where one wants references to the roadmap in the code and the other does not), and we should presumably clarify the rubrics to avoid such incompatibilities.

In other cases, it seems to me like the goals themselves are not incompatible, but merely the most obvious proposed fixes are (e.g., reuse asks for something to be public and api-design asks for that same thing to be private). In such cases, the best fix is often a larger change that addresses the two underlying concerns (in one such example, they were both happy with refactoring things to use a more general public lemma).

Sometimes my author agents think of such a broader change on their own, but other times it helps for me to mention the general idea of doing such (even without a specific proposed change). Hence I think it might be helpful for the review agents to specify their underlying concerns based on their rubric separately from their suggested fix (making it clear that the latter is merely one possible approach). This might cause the author agents to be more creative on their own, and reduce the number of appeals of the form "but you told me to do this''.

(It might also be helpful for review agents to be able to see the relevant findings from other review agents without the author having to send them, but I worry that this might change their behavior in other bad ways, while it feels likely harmless to me for the reviews themselves to simply separate the underlying concerns from the proposed fix.)

@Kim Morrison The issues discussed here are affecting many PRs, causing review churn. Particularly TauCetiReview#130, for which I have asked my agent (astra) to summarize the impact to PRs my agent reviewed and additional PRs across math areas, models, reviewer etc. as a comment to the issue with additional findings. May you review the surgical PR TauCetiReview#131 by @Fabian Zaiser ?

In the comment, my agent also find out that even after explicitly excluding roadmap, the attribution rubric may still cause a review agent to require attributions to Suggested.lean which is not desired too.

In one of the contests from the author agent, the author agent even learned to cite issue 130 as a reason.

@Utensil Song Thanks! I noticed my agent citing #130 too, but I don't think it's effective. If I understand correctly, the _reviewing agent has no internet access_ and can just see the checkout of the repo at the PR + some comments on the PR. So citing another issue doesn't help because the reviewer cannot check and is instructed to treat the PR author as an adversary.

I have asked my agent to check TauCetiReview#132, added a comment on impacts on PRs my agent reviewed, and concured the proposed fix.

The situation for TauCetiReview#133 is more complicated, the agent picked the first proposed fix (make api-design own the call), with an dedup exception, also noted that proof-quality rubric may start the cycle again.
I have opened TauCetiReview#134 to address TauCetiReview#132. I try to keep its wording changes minimal, and have put them under stress tests of the PRs mentioned in the issue, they seem to stand.

TauCetiReview#135 was also opened to address TauCetiReview#133, and put to stress test (142 review runs), however it is trickier and I don't seem to be able to make it pass. The PR now stays as a draft and the comment provides the remaining failure patterns on the stress test.
@Kim Morrison This is causing a lot of wasteful back-and-forth on many PRs. I'd appreciate it if you could look at least at my (very small) proposed fix TauCetiReview#131.
So I've approved it but it will also need Kim's approval

A couple of TauCeti PR's were stuck in an infinite review loop:

https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/6472: 191 comments
https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/6873: 84 comments
(https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/6869: 85 comments.
https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/6147 : 120 comments

There is a conflict between the repair worker prompt which says “Everything under namespace TauCeti.” and the naming reviewer which requires declarations extending existing Mathlib types to live in their root namespaces (CovariantDerivative, RingEquiv, or Set) so receiver dot notation works. So the repair agent agrees with the reviewer but refuses to make the change, and the loop begins anew. I intervened on the first three allowing my agent to use Mathlib namespaces. Also I submitted a PR to modify the prompts for the repair agent. https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker/pull/220

@Erik (√2, sqrt-of-2):

https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/8690 is stuck because it seems your review agents are running with an outdated snapshot of the review rubrics. I don't know exactly how you'd go about refreshing it, but I though I should let you know.

This might be a symptom of a problem with the review runner code, though. Ideally the runner should dynamically fetch the freshest possible rubrics before review unless explicitly overridden for development purposes. This might be something for @Kim Morrison to look in to.

I set up an issue for this here:

https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiReview/issues/144

Sorry about the delays here.

@Ryan McCorvie, I've now merged TauCetiWorker#220, about dot-notation namespaces.

(It's worth noting that it is actually okay to put something in e.g. TauCeti.Lean.Expr.foo, and dot notation still works, since lean4#6189 (way back in 2024!) but my personal preference is to nevertheless put such things in Lean.Expr.foo. We want the namespace collisions to hit us if upstream adds these things!)

@Utensil Song, pinging on TauCetiReview#134, where I have asked you to drop a sentence, but I'm otherwise happy. If I don't hear from you I'll just delete the sentence myself and merge this. I'm assuming that TauCetiReview#135 is intentionally still in draft: let me know if you'd like me to be thinking about this, or otherwise let's close it.

@Kim Morrison sorry I missed the review on GitHub. For TauCetiReview#134, the issue is 2-fold:

The change on the reuse rubric is to ask the agent to come up with more evidence (e.g. which public theorem provided the same access) before claiming duplication, so the review agent would be less trigger-happy when they see potential duplication, characteristic lemmas are the most frequent victims.

On the other hand we also need to ask the agent to refrain itself on the api-design rubric, so it should only demand such lemma when it is sure that is no existing theorem providing the same access.

Admittedly the wording in api-design is too concise so now its purpose is beyond recognition, they were simplified from the initial verbose version which may make more sense?

However, I'm happy to drop it and observe the effect if we only fix one side of the problem: allowing api-design to request the trivial restate while suppressing reuse to claim duplication. This would definitely settle the dispute between review agents, I was just concerned that this is not the desired balance.

For TauCetiReview#135, the PR is intentionally still in draft, because it is a more delicate matter, and I explained the reason here. I can't fully make the sympton described in the issue disappear by tweaking wording. So extra eyes on it would be appreciated. The draft PR demonstrates an unsuccessful attempt.

:robot: Claude says: @Utensil Song, thanks, that makes sense. Since you're happy to, let's drop the api-design sentence and keep the reuse change, then see whether the reuse side alone settles the disputes. If api-design keeps demanding restatements that an existing public theorem already gives access to, we can come back with clearer wording for that side. I'll merge TauCetiReview#134 once the sentence is gone (or drop it myself if that's easier).

:robot: Claude says: @Harald Husum, TauCetiReview#144 is fixed by TauCetiReview#161. Before each review the CLI now compares its rubrics with the published main. If they differ (an out-of-date or pinned checkout, or local edits), it warns the operator, and the posted scoreboard and review threads carry a :warning: note, so a PR author contesting a finding can see that the rubrics might be out of date. It no longer links to a rubrics commit that isn't on GitHub. Reviews still post either way, so testing rubric changes keeps working. (The standard worker refreshes the rubrics every round, so it was never affected.)
@Utensil Song, okay, yes, so far I am skeptical about #135.

For TauCetiReview#134, I have just asked Astra to comment with the result of re-evaluating the effect of the sentence in api-design on PRs reviewed by my fork which merged 134 a while ago. Apparently that sentence is too concise to prevent what it intended to prevent and the resue side seems to be effective. Thus we have pushed a commit to drop the api-design side for now.
